title: Sharing is leaking: blocking transient-execution attacks with core-gapped confidential VMs
problem: Confidential VMs are vulnerable to transient-execution attacks because CPU cores with complex microarchitectural state are multiplexed among distrusting entities controlled by an untrusted hypervisor. Shared microarchitectural resources enable information leakage through side-channel attacks.
motivation: Confidential VMs promise security against hypervisor-level attackers but this security guarantee has been repeatedly broken by transient-execution vulnerabilities and CPU bugs.
method: The paper proposes core-gapped confidential VMs that isolate CPU cores to prevent microarchitectural state sharing and multiplexing among distrusting entities. By dedicating cores exclusively to individual VMs rather than sharing them, the architecture blocks transient-execution attacks that exploit shared cache and microarchitectural side-channels.
key_novelty: Using core isolation and gapping to eliminate microarchitectural resource sharing as a defense mechanism against transient-execution attacks in confidential VMs.
contributions: Identifies core multiplexing and microarchitectural state sharing as the root cause of transient-execution vulnerabilities in confidential VMs
Proposes core-gapped confidential VM architecture to prevent cross-tenant information leakage
Demonstrates blocking of transient-execution attacks through architectural isolation
limitations: Limitations not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Confidential VM security via core isolation
